what_it_does: When designing and checking chips, engineers need to recognize complex structures in the circuit (like full adders, which add three bits together) buried in millions of logic gates. BoolE is a new technique that uses equality saturation—a method that finds all mathematically equivalent ways to express the same logic—and applies Boolean algebra rules to simplify and restructure gate-level netlists. Once equivalent forms are organized in an 'e-graph' (a structure that groups all equivalent expressions), a novel extraction algorithm identifies multi-input, multi-output building blocks that weren't obvious in the original gate layout. This helps design tools understand what they're looking at and work more efficiently.
